keyframe_review.note: New keyframe (no Cliopatria row; the Han Dynasty, Cao Wei and Western Jin shapes contain the land). The page lists seven counties (Daifang, Liekou, Nanxin, Changcen, Tixi, Hanzi, Haiming) and no boundaries, and carries no area or infobox, so no area comparison could be made. The page says Jin 'lost control of the peninsula at the start of the 4th century'; the last Jin years are drawn as Daifang's because the page gives 314 for the conquest.

region.text: Daifang, 'located around Hwanghae' (Daifang page), cut from the southern half of Lelang

ledger.note: 204: Gongsun Kang cuts Daifang from Lelang's southern half. Four Commanderies page: 'Gongsun Kang created it in 204'; the Daifang page: 'established the Daifang Commandery sometime between 204 and 220 CE to make administration more efficient'; the Gongsun Kang page: 'Around this time' after 204, 'by separating the southern half from the Lelang commandery'.

238: Daifang passes from the Gongsun to Cao Wei. 'In 238 CE, under the order of Emperor Ming of Cao Wei, Sima Yi defeated the Gongsun family and annexed Liaodong, Lelang and Daifang to Wei.' The commandery keeps its colony tint; the metropole becomes cao-wei.
265: Daifang passes to the Jin. 'Daifang Commandery was inherited by the Jin dynasty.' The page gives no year; 265, the start of Cliopatria's Western Jin, is a bridge.

region.text: Daifang, 'located around Hwanghae' (Daifang page), cut from the southern half of Lelang

ledger.note: 314: Goguryeo conquers Daifang. 'It was conquered by Goguryeo in 314 CE.' After Luoyang fell to the Xiongnu in 311, Zhang Tong 'went for help to Murong Hui ... with his subjects in 314'. The Four Commanderies page has 314-315 for the end; the Goguryeo dossier (jk-02-b) has Micheon attacking Daifang in 314 in a note but no gain event, which should be added.

region.text: Daifang, 'located around Hwanghae' (Daifang page), cut from the southern half of Lelang

ledger.note: 314: the southern commandery ends. 'Goguryeo under King Micheon annexed Lelang and Daifang soon after' Luoyang's fall (Daifang page).

wars.name: Goguryeo-Wei War
wars.outcome: Cao Wei victory; Gong Zun, grand administrator of Daifang, marched south with Liu Mao of Lelang through the Seven Counties of Lingdong and six counties submitted; afterwards the Ye and Okjeo tributaries returned to the influence of Lelang and Daifang.
wars.note: No territory of Daifang changed hands; the Ye vassal tint is carried in the lelang-commandery ledger.

wars.name: Goguryeo conquest of Lelang and Daifang

notes: Colony dossier; no Cliopatria row. The Han (to 206), Cao Cao (207..223), Cao Wei (224..264) and Western Jin (265..312) shapes already contain this land, so the renderer must let the commandery's tint win or the metropole dossiers must subtract it. The seat is a placeholder. The Daifang page is silent on Mahan, Baekje, the Japanese envoys (Himiko, 238-247) and the Han River; nothing in it reaches south of Hwanghae. Baekje's northern frontier (the 369-371 Baekje-Goguryeo war in the baekje dossier) is not on the pages opened here. The 244-245 war moved no Daifang border, so no contest is recorded. The goguryeo dossier needs a 314 gain from daifang-commandery and a 319 gain from xuantu-commandery.
